doc.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Voice and bass performances with Kenny Peplowski
summary: They discuss his vocal-and-bass sets, the challenge of keeping solo concerts interesting, and playing with clarinetist Kenny Peplowski.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well when you did your thing last night, your set last night, I mean in my opinion at these parties, it was a great change of pace, it was really something different, I really enjoyed it.
And just the vocal note, with your bass line, those two things moving, great stuff.

Yeah. I enjoy it. You know if you can get it to sound decent you can have a lot of fun with just being at the top and the bottom of Bach, leaving the middle two lines to someone else, you know you’re the lead and the bass. And I mean I’ve done concerts of just myself, and it’s great fun. And I’ve not gotten a bad review from it, because you’ve got to do awfully interesting material however. You’ve got to find ways to make it very interesting for the audience because you’re going to walk out there with a bass, so you’ve got to have some interesting patter and have some fun and keep the songs flowing so their ears don’t get totally exhausted by bass — voice — bass — voice. So you’ve got to find ways to get around things. And having Kenny Peplowski play with me of course is — what a player, what a sound he gets out of that clarinet. What a sound.
